ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The table lists the plant height and light saturation point of 4 crops A, B, C, and D. A has a plant height of 170 cm and a light saturation point of 1200 μmol·m^-2·s^-1; B has a plant height of 65 cm and a light saturation point of 1180 μmol·m^-2·s^-1; C has a plant height of 59 cm and a light saturation point of 560 μmol·m^-2·s^-1; D has a plant height of 165 cm and a light saturation point of 623 μmol·m^-2·s^-1. Reasoning: When intercropping improves light energy utilization efficiency, crops with large differences in plant height should be selected to form upper- and lower-layer complementary canopies; tall-stemmed crops are located in the upper layer and should be adapted to strong light, that is, have a high light saturation point; short-stemmed crops are located in the lower layer and should be adapted to weak light, that is, have a low light saturation point. A is both tall-stemmed and has a high light saturation point, suitable for using strong light in the upper layer; C is both short-stemmed and has a low light saturation point, suitable for using weak light in the lower layer. Therefore, the most suitable for intercropping are A and C.
